Uzbekistan Grapples with Soaring Inflation as Som Loses Value

TASHKENT – Uzbekistan is facing a rapidly worsening economic crisis as the national currency, the som, has lost more than 30% of its value against the US dollar over the past two months, triggering a wave of inflation and uncertainty for businesses and households across the country.

The Central Bank of Uzbekistan’s emergency measures, including raising interest rates and intervening in currency markets, have so far failed to halt the som’s slide. Official figures released Thursday show annual inflation reaching 21%, with food prices climbing even faster. In Tashkent’s Chorsu Bazaar, shoppers and vendors alike voiced concern as staples like flour, sugar, and cooking oil have doubled in price since early April.

“We cannot keep up with these prices. Every week, something is more expensive,” said Dilshod Karimov, a shopkeeper in the capital. “People buy less, and some cannot afford basic items anymore.”

The crisis has hit importers particularly hard, as the cost of foreign goods has jumped with the weaker som. Diyorbek Trading, an importer of electronics, announced it has suspended new orders due to price volatility. “We cannot plan when we don’t know what the exchange rate will be tomorrow,” said company director Gavkhar Turaeva.

The government has pledged to protect the most vulnerable. President Shavkat Mirziyoev addressed the nation Wednesday, promising expanded subsidies for low-income families and direct support for small businesses. “We are working with our partners to stabilize the economy and safeguard our citizens,” he said.

However, economists warn that more structural reforms may be needed. “This is a test for Uzbekistan’s economic resilience,” said Timur Ismailov, an analyst at the Central Asia Policy Institute. “Restoring confidence will require transparency and tough decisions in the coming weeks.”

The som’s instability continues to affect daily life, with no immediate end in sight.
